irrătĭōnābĭlis (inr- ), e, adj.,
I.without reason, irrational (post-class.; not in Quint., v. Spald. ad Quint. 2, 16, 16): “error,” App. Dogm. Plat. p. 21 : “motus,” Amm. 31, 12, 15 .— Of musical intervals, = logica, proportional, harmonic: “irrationabilia (sunt) quibus non subest ratio,” Mart. Cap. 9, § 949 .—Subst.: irrătĭōnābĭlĭa , ĭum, n., unreasoning creatures, Lact. 2, 2, 17.— Adv.: irrătĭōnābĭlĭter , irrationally, Amm. 19, 10, 1; Tert. Poen. 2; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 199.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
